Upgrading a server under a live app is usually an evening, a maintenance window and an apology in advance.
My three servers run two copies of every part of the app, placed so no two copies of the same thing share a machine. A rule tells the cluster it may never take both down at once.

So the upgrade is a button. The cluster drains the first server, which means it moves every running copy to the other two machines, the server reboots on the new version, and the copies come back. Then I do the same to the other two.

Nobody on the other end sees it.
Try that with Docker Compose on three boxes. You are the load balancer, the health check and the traffic switch, at eleven at night.
